messages:
Ana: Quick heads-up — planning a canary for the multi-region failover routing toggle TOMORROW 06:00 UTC.
Goal: validate fallback to eu-west when us-west is saturated. Canary: 5% traffic, mode: per-request for the canary (not session-sticky). Need eng-platform + oncall to ack and own monitoring for first 30m.

Mira: Quick q — session stickiness across regions: we currently use cookie-based stickiness on the edge LB. If fallback routes mid-session, we’ll lose KV affinity and that can spike latency/miss rate.

Lee: Prefer per-request for the 5% canary to avoid huge cache-miss storms. Keep session-sticky only for any staged rollout >20%.

Sam: :thumbsup: Also suggest guardrails: auto-rollback if backend error_rate > 1% for 5m OR p95 latency increases by >300ms vs baseline.

Ana: Got it. I’ll create the feature flag entry routing.multi_region_failover with scope=canary(5%) and mode=per_request. Will flip via internal FF service and post the exact CLI command here.

Ana: flip command (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flag":"routing.multi_region_failover","action":"enable","canary_pct":5,"mode":"per_request","meta":{"canary_window":"06:00-06:30 UTC","owner":"ana"}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag routing.multi_region_failover created in staging (id=ff-8732). No rollout to prod yet.

Mira: Who’s on metrics watch? I can take first 30 minutes (06:00-06:30). @Lee can pick up second half.

Lee: I’ll watch p95 latency, overall error rate, redis miss_rate, and model.region_fallback_count. Also check token-generation tail latency.

Sam: Add an alert threshold: if model.region_fallback_count > 0.5% of requests for 3m then pager. Also add a dashboard widget for 
- routing.fallback_count
- routing.p95_latency_delta
- cache.miss_rate

Mira: Agree. I’ll add an ephemeral alarm tied to the flag scope so it only applies during the canary window.

Ana: Quick smoke tests after flip:
1) curl <edge>/health  -> 200
2) run 50 synthetic requests with session-id header -> check distribution
3) check logs for session->region mapping for anomalies

Lee: Also watch for client 5xx spikes (edge) and model 503s. If we see any client 5xx > 0.5% in 5m, rollback.

Sam: Adding a quick rollback command to run if needed:
```
# rollback to disable
curl -X POST https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flag":"routing.multi_region_failover","action":"disable","reason":"auto-rollback or manual"}'
```

Mira: I'll own executing rollback if alarms fire and will notify oncall.

Ana: Plan summary: 06:00 UTC toggle -> smoke checks -> 06:05 verify metrics -> if green, keep 5% for 60m -> bump to 20% at ~07:00 (manual) assuming no guardrail trips. I’ll post status updates here.

Lee: sgtm. Ping @oncall if anything looks off.

Mira: :eyes: standing by. Will annotate the dashboard and leave the ephemeral alarm live for the canary window.

Sam: One last note — ensure KV prefix invalidation isn't triggered globally. Set cache-affinity TTL drops to 10s for the canary to reduce cross-region staleness.

Ana: Thanks all. I’ll post the final toggle time and the exact monitoring links ~1hr before. Tagging deploy-bot to automate creation of the ephemeral alarm.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: ephemeral alarm created (id=alarm-546), dashboard links posted in #dash-links.

Ana: Thanks — will keep updates short here. If anyone has concerns before EOD please shout now.
